newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- ends up 1/4 to 3/8 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- ends up 1/4 to 3/8 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were up about 1/4 to 3/8 in late Thursday trading, finishing near the day's highs amid a stronger Treasury market.
The government long bond was up 10/32 at 94-15/32 to yield 7.07 percent, after trading at 7.05 percent earlier in the day.
Despite the government market's late day move off its highs, munis managed to keep most of the day's gains, traders said.

The futures markets, however, finished below their best readings. The June municipal contract closed up 11/32 to 112-20/32 and June T-bonds were 12/32 higher at 107-27/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 153 ticks from 154 at the close on Wednesday.

In secondary market activity, Delaware River Port Authority FGIC-insured 5-1/2s of 2026 were bid at 5.86 percent, up one basis point. Jefferson County, Ala., FGIC 5-3/4s of 2027 were unchanged at 96-1/2, after trading up 1/8 at midday.
In the day's limited new issue action, Morgan Stanley & Co. said it repriced Tucson Electric Power Co.'s $132 million revenue bond deal. The top yield at the repricing was 7.125 percent in 2032.

After a fairly modest week of new issues, next week is expected to see a pickup. A preliminary tally of the week's volume showed about $3.2 billion of new deals, mostly on the negotiated calendar. The largest is a $920 million deal from the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, through Lehman Brothers.
Friday's data releases include the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment survey for April at 1000 EDT. The report is expected to show a reading of 99.8, compared to 100 the previous month.
